challenges.name: versioned-score-update-quiz
challenges.title: Is this update really newer?
challenges.description: Two pieces of evidence from the score consumer: a Lua script that compares versions, and a timeline of two workers that check before they write.

questions.question:
The consumer applies { learnerId, totalScore, version } with this script (KEYS[1] = lb:all, KEYS[2] = lb:ver, ARGV = learnerId, totalScore, version):

local stored = redis.call('HGET', KEYS[2], ARGV[1])
if stored and stored >= ARGV[3] then
  return 'skipped'
end
redis.call('ZADD', KEYS[1], ARGV[2], ARGV[1])
redis.call('HSET', KEYS[2], ARGV[1], ARGV[3])
return 'applied'

Consumer log for u_2290:

10:41:07.112 v9  total 300 -> applied
10:41:52.840 v10 total 340 -> skipped
10:42:30.005 v11 total 380 -> skipped

> HGET lb:ver u_2290
"9"

Statement: "Versions 10 and 11 are skipped because the script compares the versions as strings, and \"9\" sorts after \"10\" and \"11\"."
questions.explanation: True. HGET returns a bulk string and ARGV values are strings, so Lua's >= compares them character by character: "9" >= "10" is true because '9' comes after '1'. Every version from 10 to 89 now looks older than 9, so the learner's score is frozen at 300 until version 90. The fix is tonumber() on both sides (or storing a fixed-width version). The misconception is that Redis knows the hash value is a number: everything in a hash is a string, and the comparison follows the types of the language that does it.

False. Each command is atomic on its own, but the check (HGET) and the write (ZADD, HSET) are separate round trips, and another worker can run in between. At t2 worker B read version 14 before A wrote 16, so B still believes v15 is newer and overwrites 410 with 380 - and even moves the stored version back to 15. Check and write must be one unit: a Lua script (EVAL/EVALSHA), or WATCH lb:ver + MULTI/EXEC with a retry when EXEC returns null. The misconception is that atomic commands make a sequence of commands atomic.

challenges.name: versioned-score-updates
challenges.title: Apply only newer score updates
challenges.description:
CodeDev's leaderboard consumer applies score updates from PostgreSQL to the Redis board. After each graded submission, PostgreSQL recomputes the learner's total and increments learner_score.version in the same transaction; an outbox relay then sends { learnerId, totalScore, version }. Two consumer workers read the stream and the relay retries, so an update can arrive twice, and an older update can arrive after a newer one. The shipped consumer did ZADD for every message: a slow worker put a learner back from 340 to 300 points, and a learner who had hidden themselves from the leaderboard reappeared. totalScore null means the learner left the board (show_on_leaderboard turned off, or the account deleted).

Write applyUpdate(redis, update). Keys: lb:all is the sorted set (member = learnerId, score = totalScore); lb:ver is a hash, field = learnerId, value = the last applied version as a decimal string. The update comes from JSON, so check it at runtime. Return:
- "invalid" when learnerId is not a non-empty string, version is not a positive safe integer, or totalScore is neither null nor a safe integer >= 0. Nothing changes.
- "duplicate" when version equals the stored version (the same database row again; the payload is not compared). Nothing changes.
- "stale" when version is lower than the stored version. Nothing changes.
- "applied" when version is higher, or the learner has no stored version (counts as 0; members written before versions existed have none): ZADD the total - a total of 0 is a score, not a removal - or ZREM the learner when totalScore is null, and store the version in lb:ver, also for a removal, so an older update that arrives later cannot bring the learner back.
Compare versions as numbers: lb:ver holds strings, and "9" must be lower than "10". The protocol must not depend on arrival order: any order of the same updates must end with the same lb:all and lb:ver. In production the check and the writes run as one Lua script; the in-memory model in the starter is single-threaded, so plain calls are enough here.

Input (stdin): { "initial"?: { "board"?: [[learnerId, score]], "versions"?: [[learnerId, version]] }, "updates": [update], "orders"?: k, "summary"?: true }. Output: one line per update with its outcome, the board (member count, then ranks) and the stored versions sorted by learner id; with orders, whether k other orders of the same updates end the same; with summary, a count per outcome instead of the per-update lines, and only the top 10. Do not change the types, FakeClock, FakeRedis or the test runner.
hints: For one learner, which single number tells you whether an incoming update is newer than what the board shows - and where must that number live so that it is still there after the learner has left the board?

Look at what hget returns (a string or null) and how you compare it with the incoming version, at what you write to lb:ver when totalScore is null, and at how you tell a total of 0 apart from a removal.

The same protocol on a different board, course ratings: hash rating:ver, sorted set rating:avg, stored version "8" for course c_12. Updates arrive: v12 avg 45 -> 12 > 8, ZADD and store "12"; v9 avg 41 -> 9 < 12, stale (compared as strings, "9" would look newer than "12"); v12 again -> duplicate; v13 with avg null (course unpublished) -> ZREM and store "13"; v10 avg 43 arriving last -> stale, and the course stays off the list.
